fields.description: Which records are measured. A Link to DocType and not a Select of two: a target over a job, a ticket or an application is the same row, and a CRM is only where somebody asked for it first.
fields.label: Applies to

fields.description: Which target wins when two of them fit. Lowest first, so the narrow one goes above the catch-all.
fields.label: Order

fields.description: A fieldname on the doctype above whose value picks a row from the levels below. Left blank, every record gets the default level — which is right for a desk that promises everybody the same thing.
fields.label: Priority is in

fields.description: Every rule has to hold. Empty means the target covers all of that doctype.
fields.label: Only when

fields.description: Days the clock does not run at all. ERPNext's own, so a workspace keeps one list for payroll, projects and this.
fields.label: Holiday list

fields.description: Empty means every day, all day — which is the honest reading of a desk that has not said otherwise, and is what a support line that runs at night actually wants.
fields.label: Working days

fields.description: One row where everybody is promised the same thing; one per priority where they are not.
fields.label: Priorities

fields.description: The best idea in Frappe CRM's agreement. With this on, somebody writing back after an answer starts the clock again — because an agreement is about a conversation and not about one email. Off, only the first reply is measured.
fields.label: Every reply, not just the first

fields.description: What counts as dealt with, in the same rule shape as `applies_when`: a deal whose stage category is Won or Lost, a job whose status is Closed. Empty means the resolution clock is never stopped by the record itself and somebody says so by hand.
fields.label: Settled when
